s.t:
💻 Nous positionner sur le marché comme un éditeur de solution de comptabilité et de gestion financière innovant
💰 Lever un total de 400 millions d'euros, auprès d'investisseurs de renom, dont Sequoïa, le fonds phare de la Silicon Valley, connu pour avoir soutenu Google, Facebook, Airbnb, Stripe, Paypal et bien d'autres à leur début

🚀 Déjà plus de 900,000 TPE/PME et plus de 6000 cabinets d’expertise-comptable utilisent Pennylane en France !
Pourquoi ce rôle est-il si important chez nous ?
Notre solution est l'outil de travail principal de nos cabinets comptables, partenaires et dirigeants. La qualité du travail de ces utilisateurs dépend donc grandement de la qualité de notre solution.
En qualité d’expert du support technique, tu es garant de la fiabilité et la bonne utilisation quotidienne de la plateforme Pennylane.
Tu es entre autres responsable des sujets les plus techniques, qui peuvent avoir un impact très important sur la satisfaction client et sur l'image de Pennylane.
Comment vas-tu contribuer au projet ?
Tu es à la fois un référent fonctionnel comptable et un point de contact clé entre nos utilisateurs, les équipes support, produit et les développeurs.
Grâce à ta double compétence comptable et technique, tu accompagnes l’analyse des problématiques rencontrées par les utilisateurs sur la plateforme, qu’elles soient liées à des sujets métiers, fonctionnels ou techniques.
Tu investigues les incidents remontés via les tickets, identifies leur origine, évalues leur criticité et coordonnes leur résolution avec les équipes concernées. Tu assures également un suivi clair et régulier auprès des différentes parties prenantes.
Le poste demande autant de rigueur analytique que de communication : tu échanges quotidiennement avec plusieurs équipes internes et contribues directement à l’amélioration continue du produit et de l’expérience utilisateur.
Quelles seront tes missions au quotidien ?
Gestion, investigation et suivi des tickets
Prendre en charge les tickets remontés par les utilisateurs ou partenaires (bugs, investigations, anomalies fonctionnelles ou comptables), analyser et diagnostiquer les incidents, prioriser les demandes selon leur impact et coordonner leur résolution avec les équipes concernées.
Expertise produit & accompagnement métier
Maîtriser les principales fonctionnalités et modules de la plateforme afin de comprendre les cas d’usage clients, reproduire les problématiques rencontrées et accompagner les utilisateurs sur des sujets comptables et fonctionnels.
Coordination avec les équipes internes
Collaborer étroitement avec les développeurs, équipes produit, support et opérations pour assurer une résolution rapide et durable des problèmes identifiés.
Analyse technique
Être capable d’investiguer des problématiques techniques simples via les outils mis à disposition (API, logs, Postman, SQL basique), comprendre les échanges techniques avec les développeurs et faciliter la communication entre équipes métier et tech.
Documentation & amélioration continue
Formaliser les solutions, process et bonnes pratiques dans la base de connaissances afin d’améliorer la qualité du support et fluidifier la résolution future des incidents.
Identifier les problématiques récurrentes, remonter les tendances observées et participer activement à l’amélioration continue du produit et des process internes.
Entraide & partage de connaissances
Participer à la montée en compétence des membres de l’équipe, partager les bonnes pratiques et contribuer à une culture collaborative et orientée résolution.

· Tu justifies d’au moins 3 ans d'expérience sur un pote similaire dans un environnement SaaS, support client ou support fonctionnel/technique
· Tu disposes d’une bonne compréhension des outils techniques : API REST, Postman, Swagger (des connaissances SQL sont un plus)

Support Engineer
Edinburgh
Wordsmith
Wordsmith is building the legal operating system for in-house teams, and we are growing fast.
We believe in-house legal is becoming one of the most important functions in the AI era. Every business is moving faster, but legal work is still too often scattered across inboxes, chats, documents and disconnected systems.
Wordsmith brings that work into one system. Requests come in from across the business, AI agents handle the routine, lawyers stay in control where judgement matters, and every step is captured as work happens.
We are built for in-house legal, not law firms. Our goal is to help legal teams move faster, reduce unnecessary external counsel spend and become a function the business can run with.
More than 500 companies, including Financial Times, Safelite, Trip.com , Canva, Starling and Sage, use Wordsmith. Backed by over $100M from Index Ventures, General Catalyst, Highland Europe and others, we are building one of the defining companies in legal AI.

We’re hiring a Support Engineer to provide fast, thoughtful and technically rigorous help to Wordsmith customers.
You’ll own technical questions and incidents from first response through to resolution. You’ll understand what the customer is trying to achieve, reproduce reported behaviour, investigate the underlying cause and explain the outcome clearly.
This is more than scripted customer support. You’ll be expected to investigate application behaviour at a technical level, including reading logs and tracing issues through the product and its codebase. Where appropriate to your experience, you may also propose and submit code fixes through our normal engineering review and release process.
Wordsmith supports customers globally through a follow-the-sun model. You’ll work the standard hours for your region and hand over unresolved issues clearly to colleagues in other regions. There is no routine expectation that you work another region’s hours.

Own technical support requests — triage, investigate and resolve customer questions and incidents from first response to confirmed resolution.
Diagnose problems thoroughly — gather the right context, reproduce reported behaviour, inspect logs and data, and trace issues through the product and codebase.
Resolve technical issues — correct configuration or usage problems directly and collaborate with Engineering when a product or infrastructure change is required.
Contribute code fixes where appropriate — depending on your experience, propose and submit well-tested fixes through the standard engineering review and deployment process.
Communicate clearly — give customers timely and accurate updates, explain technical issues without unnecessary jargon and set honest expectations.
Manage escalations — bring in Engineering, Product or other specialists when needed while retaining ownership of the case and its communication.
Support global handovers — document investigation, impact, current status and next actions so colleagues in another region can continue work without losing momentum.
Protect service quality — recognise high-impact incidents quickly, follow the appropriate escalation process and contribute to incident reviews.
Build customer knowledge — create and maintain troubleshooting guides, known-issue documentation and help-centre content.
Reduce repeat problems — identify patterns in support demand and recommend improvements to the product, documentation, tooling and customer experience.
Improve support operations — help develop service levels, escalation paths, reporting and technical-support processes as the function scales.

Experience in technical support, product support, software engineering, solutions engineering or another customer-facing technical role.
Strong diagnostic ability — you can work methodically from symptoms to root cause rather than relying on guesswork.
A working understanding of modern web applications, APIs, authentication, integrations and common browser or network issues.
Experience using diagnostic information such as application logs, monitoring tools, browser developer tools and database queries.
Enough familiarity with software code to navigate a codebase, follow application logic and use it to investigate reported behaviour.
Clear customer communication — you can remain calm under pressure, set expectations honestly and explain complex issues at the right level of detail.
Strong ownership — you remain responsible for moving an issue forward even when other teams need to contribute.
Sound prioritisation — you can assess urgency and customer impact and recognise when an issue requires immediate escalation.
Care and precision — you document what you tested, avoid unsupported conclusions and confirm that the customer’s problem has actually been resolved.
Interest in AI systems — you’re curious about how AI-enabled products behave and comfortable investigating issues that may not always be deterministic.
No legal background is required, but you should be motivated to learn how in-house legal teams work.
Desirable, but not essential
Experience writing and debugging production software.
The ability to create automated tests and submit code fixes for engineering review.
Experience supporting AI-enabled or data-intensive applications.
Familiarity with incident-management and observability tools.
How we work
We’re an in-person team based in Edinburgh. You should expect to work from the office as your default.
We support customers globally using a follow-the-sun model. You’ll work the normal hours agreed for your region and create clear handovers when an issue needs to continue beyond them. Any exceptional on-call or out-of-hours arrangements would be agreed and communicated separately.
We set a high bar, move quickly and give people meaningful ownership. Support is a core part of the product experience, and we expect it to be technically credible, responsive and human.
You’ll work closely with Engineering, Product, Transformation and Customer Success. Customer Success owns adoption and customer health; Transformation owns implementation; Account Management owns renewals and commercial growth; and Support Engineering owns technical investigation and resolution.
Why Wordsmith
You’ll support a fast-growing product used for important work inside some of the world’s most ambitious organisations.
Because we’re building in a new technical category, the problems are interesting. You’ll work across software behaviour, integrations, data and AI systems rather than following a script.
You’ll have the opportunity to shape our support tooling and operating model, influence the product through direct customer evidence, and develop towards senior support engineering, support leadership, solutions engineering or product engineering.

Why an IT apprenticeship at Accenture could be the perfect fit for you? Because you-ll be working in a cool, open-minded team-at one of the world-s leading consulting and technology companies! At Accenture, you-ll find countless opportunities to develop your skills and move step by step toward your career goals.
During your four-year apprenticeship at our Zurich location, you-ll not only learn a lot but also immerse yourself in exciting projects with our clients.

The world of IT is waiting for you-are you ready to shape it? In your apprenticeship as an application developer, you-ll dive deep into digital transformation. You-ll learn how to develop software, program apps, and design innovative solutions for complex challenges.
Your journey begins with two intensive years of training at our partner companies, Noser Young AG or TIE International AG in Zurich. After that, you-ll join Accenture and enter the exciting world of IT consulting, where you-ll apply your knowledge in real-world projects.
**Your daily work**
* **Shape the digital future with us.**
IT is essential in today-s world! At Accenture, you-ll have the chance to learn this exciting profession and contribute to digitalization projects.
* **Learn programming languages and develop your own software.**
You-ll get hands-on experience with different programming languages, app development, and software design. Additionally, you-ll learn how to maintain applications and provide optimal support.
* **Find the best IT solutions for our clients.**
As an application developer, you-ll identify client needs, analyze their current situation, and propose solutions along with their advantages and disadvantages.
* **Start your apprenticeship with a strong partner.**
The first two years of your training will take place at our training partners, Noser Young AG or TIE International AG, in Zurich. Afterwards, you-ll gain practical experience in IT consulting at Accenture through real-world projects.
* **Immerse yourself in the world of IT and application development.**
You-ll be part of a dynamic team, collaborating with colleagues and gradually deepening your expertise in IT and application development.

s.h: NOTRE ENGAGEMENT EN FAVEUR DE L'INCLUSION ET DE L'ACCESSIBILITE
s.t:
Chez Decathlon, nous reconnaissons l'immense valeur qu'apporte la diversité à nos équipes et nous nous efforçons continuellement de favoriser et de cultiver un lieu de travail inclusif et équitable : c'est pourquoi l'Inclusion est l'un de nos Fondamentaux Humains.

Nous encourageons les personnes de tous horizons et de toutes capacités à postuler, car nous sommes convaincu·es que la diversité des pensées, des cultures, des identités et des expériences vécues nous rend plus fort·es. Decathlon s'engage également à offrir un processus de sélection inclusif et accessible à tous les candidat·es.

En cas de besoin d'aménagement, tu peux en faire la demande via le formulaire de candidature, celle-ci sera confidentielle. Ces demandes n'affectent pas le résultat du processus de recrutement.

Imaginez si la technologie nous permettait de repousser les frontières et d'offrir des expériences sportives inédites. C'est précisément notre ambition chez Decathlon Digital ! Nous sommes une équipe de plus de 5 000 experts en ingénierie logicielle, gestion de produits, données, cloud et cybersécurité, répartis à Paris, Lille et Amsterdam.

Ensemble, nous créons la plus vaste plateforme sportive numérique, en exploitant les innovations technologiques pour optimiser la chaîne de valeur, concevoir des expériences connectées et donner une seconde vie à nos produits.
Changeons la donne pour de bon. Notre passion du sport nous guide et nous voulons qu’elle perdure. C’est pourquoi nous nous engageons à bâtir un modèle technologique plus durable, en réduisant notre impact direct sur l'environnement, et en créant un espace sûr et inclusif pour apprendre et nous épanouir ensemble. Rejoins l’équipe et façonnons le futur du sport.

As an IT Specialist (Data Science), your duties will include: Develop and implement IT data science solutions for collecting, processing, storing, managing, and integrating complex data from diverse sources to support organizational and research requirements.

Analyze large and complex data sets using statistical software, programming languages, and analytical methods to identify trends, evaluate information, and support data-driven decision-making.

Develop and maintain data visualizations, dashboards, reporting tools, and other applications that enable users to explore, analyze, interpret, and communicate data. Evaluate and apply artificial intelligence, machine learning, and other emerging technologies to improve data management, analysis, automation, and IT solutions.

Evaluate data management tools, applications, databases, cloud-based services, and other technologies to improve data integration, interoperability, quality, accessibility, and performance.

Collaborate with scientists, researchers, IT specialists, data scientists and data driven professionals, and other stakeholders to identify requirements, address technical issues, and develop data and technology solutions that support research and organizational goals.

Provide technical guidance and recommendations on data architecture, data governance, data science methods, analytical tools, and emerging technologies, and contribute to the development of data standards, strategies, and best practices.
In order to qualify for an IT Specialist (Data Science), GS-2210 position you must have: IT related experience demonstrated by paid or unpaid experience obtained in either the private or public sector, and/or completion of specific, intensive training that demonstrates all of the following four competencies: 1.

Attention to Detail - is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail; and 2.

Customer Service - Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services; and 3.

Oral Communication - Expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing oral presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately; and 4.

Problem Solving - identifies problems; determines accuracy and relevance of information; uses sound judgment to generate and evaluate alternatives, and to make recommendations In order to qualify for an IT Specialist (Data Science),GS-2210 position at the GS-12 level, you must have 1 year of specialized experience equivalent to at least the GS-11 level in the Federal service obtained in either the private or public sector typically gained in the IT field or through performing IT related tasks such as: collecting and generating data, including assisting with the design or use of surveys or other scientific instruments to collect data; curating and processing data, including performing quality checks on data sets and other information sources to identify and address data issues; preparing or supporting the dissemination of data; identifying and resolving routine data performance and management issues; storing and managing high-quality data from diverse sources for use by decision makers; and analyzing comprehensive data sets using statistical software or programming languages (e.g., R, Python) to meet established business or program requirements.

In order to qualify for an IT Specialist (Data Science),GS-2210 position at the GS-13 level, you must have 1 year of specialized experience equivalent to at least the GS-12 level in the Federal service obtained in either the private or public sector typically gained in the IT field or through performing IT related tasks such as: collecting, generating, curating, and processing data from diverse sources; designing surveys or other scientific instruments for data collection; evaluating data quality and resolving complex data performance or management issues; managing, integrating, and disseminating high-quality data to support organizational or stakeholder decision-making; and analyzing large, multidimensional, or complex data sets using statistical software or programming languages (e.g., R, Python) to derive findings and support business or program decision-making.

You will receive credit for all experience material to the position, including experience gained in religious, civic, welfare, service, and organizational activities, regardless of whether you received pay.

Do not copy and paste the duties or specialized experience from this announcement into your resume as that will not be considered a demonstration of your qualifications for this position. We may verify or assess your qualifications at any time. Inflated or unsupported qualifications may affect your rating.

Any misrepresentation or material omission of facts may be sufficient cause to end further consideration of your candidacy. Persons listed as knowing your past accomplishments or experience in your application may be contacted for verification purposes at any time. Verification may, but need not, begin before receiving an offer.

Typical work assignments include: Managing teams involved in the design, development, testing, and maintenance of large, complex, mission critical programs and applications that CBP, DHS, and stakeholder enforcement agencies use to enhance screening at U.S. ports of entry.

Developing and executing application development methods and models that incorporate new technologies, such as cloud computing and agile software methodology.

Reviewing and approving recommendations that may resolve complex issues affecting software design agency-wide and evaluates agency-wide proposals for the acquisition of software products and services.

Overseeing the testing, installation, implementation, and maintenance of application software; as well as develops and presents automation options to management that consider time, cost, and resources available agency- wide. Basic Requirement: Individuals qualifying based of experience must have Information Technology (IT) related experience demonstrating each of the four competencies listed below. Attention to Detail- Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail.

Customer Service- Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services.

Oral Communication- Expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing oral presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately.

Problem Solving- Identifies problems; determines accuracy and relevance of information; uses sound judgment to generate and evaluate alternatives, and to make recommendations. Along with the four competencies listed above you must possess at least one (1) year of specialized experience described below to qualify based on experience.

Experience: You qualify for the GS-15 grade level if you possess 1 year of specialized experience equivalent to at least the next lower grade level, performing duties such as: Leading or supervising IT software application teams responsible for the design, development, testing, implementation, maintenance, or modernization of enterprise-level applications.

Managing project teams by assigning work, setting priorities, evaluating performance, resolving issues, or recommending awards, training, or personnel actions.

Coordinating with senior leaders, program managers, business owners, technical teams, or external stakeholders to resolve complex software application, modernization, or service delivery issues.

Preparing and delivering briefings, presentations, recommendations, or decision papers for senior management on complex IT software development, acquisition, modernization, or operational support matters. NOTE: Your resume must explicitly indicate how you meet this requirement, otherwise you will be found ineligible.

Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

You must: Meet all qualification requirements, including education if applicable to this position, subject to verification at any stage of the application process; and Meet all applicable Time in Grade requirements (current federal employees must have served 52 weeks at the next lower grade or equivalent grade band in the federal service) by 09/25/2026.

If you are currently, or have been within the last 5 years, a political Schedule A, Schedule C, Non-career SES or Presidential Appointee employee in the Executive Branch, you must disclose this information to the Human Resources Office. Background Investigation: U.S.

Customs and Border Protection (CBP) is a federal law enforcement agency that requires all applicants to undergo a thorough background investigation prior to employment in order to promote the agency's core values of vigilance, service to country, and integrity.

During the screening and/or background investigation process, you will be asked questions regarding any felony criminal convictions or current felony charges, the use of illegal drugs (e.g., marijuana, cocaine, heroin, LSD, methamphetamines, ecstasy), and the use of non-prescribed controlled substances including any experimentation, possession, sale, receipt, manufacture, cultivation, production, transfer, shipping, trafficking, or distribution of controlled substances.

For additional information on the preemployment process, review the following link: Applicant Resources | CBP Careers Residency: There is a residency requirement for all applicants not currently employed by CBP.

Individuals are required to have physically resided in the United States or its protectorates (as declared under international law) for at least three of the last five years.

If you do not meet the residency requirement and you have been physically located in a foreign location for more than two of the last five years, you may request an exception to determine if you are eligible for a residency waiver by meeting one or more of the following conditions: Working for the U.S.

Government as a federal civilian or as a member of the military A dependent who was authorized to accompany a federal civilian or member of the military who was working for the U.S. government Participation in a study abroad program sponsored by a U.S. affiliated college or university Working as a contractor, intern, consultant or volunteer supporting the U.S. government Probationary Period: All employees new to the federal government must serve a one year probationary period during the first year of his/her initial permanent federal appointment to determine fitness for continued employment.

Current and former federal employees may be required to serve or complete a probationary period. Agency Career Transition Assistance Program (CTAP) or the Interagency Career Transition Assistance Program (ICTAP) Eligibles: If you have never worked for the federal government, you are not CTAP/ICTAP eligible.

View information about CTAP/ICTAP eligibility on OPM's Career Transition Resources website. To be considered well qualified under CTAP/ICTAP, you must be rated at a minimum score of 85 for this position. In addition, you must submit the supporting documents listed under the Required Documents section of this announcement.

Support report preparation and ensures effectiveness of presentation, adequacy of supporting data, and conformance with policies and standards. Conducts site visits to make sure that audits are being performed and supervised in an effective and timely manner.
